scene.name: Ball rolling down a fixed wedge into an open cup

Ball mass 0.20 kg, cup mass 1.5 kg, and fixed-body masses 100 kg are assumed; fixed-body masses do not affect their support behavior.
Friction coefficients and restitution values are assumed, not measured. Air drag is omitted. The ball is modeled as a uniform solid sphere.

source.notes: A ball sits at the top of a ramp and rolls down toward an open cup on the floor. Ramp about 1 m tall and 1.6 m long; ball about 10 cm across; cup about 50 cm wide.
explanations: The horizontal baseline is represented by a finite fixed floor platform.
The vertical edge and descending top edge define the triangular wedge profile; user clarification specifies a solid wedge fixed to the floor.
The four-sided outline depicts the ball; modeled as a sphere using the noted 0.10 m diameter.
The three strokes depict an open cup profile, modeled as a rigid cup with a base and four walls.
Dimensions follow the user notes: ramp height 1.0 m, horizontal footprint 1.6 m, ball diameter 0.10 m, cup inside opening width 0.50 m, ramp depth 0.20 m, and cup depth 0.50 m.
The ramp is modeled as a fixed solid triangular-prism wedge, as clarified. Its convex collider represents the triangular profile and uniform depth.

The cup height is inferred as 0.40 m from the drawing relative to the noted ramp height. Cup walls and base are modeled as 0.02 m-thick rigid boxes; its outer width is 0.54 m and its stated 0.50 m depth is treated as the outside depth.
The sketched baseline is modeled as a fixed 4.0 m by 2.0 m floor platform with its top at Y=0; its finite size and 0.10 m thickness are assumptions.
The ball starts at rest, touching the upper part of the wedge. The cup starts at rest on the floor and is not anchored.
Ball mass 0.20 kg, cup mass 1.5 kg, and fixed-body masses 100 kg are assumed; fixed-body masses do not affect their support behavior.
Friction coefficients and restitution values are assumed, not measured. Air drag is omitted. The ball is modeled as a uniform solid sphere.

Is the ramp a thin board supported by the upright, or a solid triangular wedge? Should the ramp/support be fixed to the floor? Also, does the stated 1.6 m ramp length mean the sloping surface length or its horizontal floor footprint? Solid wedge fixed to the floor; 1.6 m is the horizontal footprint

What depth should be used for the ramp and cup in the direction perpendicular to this side-view drawing? Is the cup’s stated 50 cm width its inside opening width? Use 0.2 m ramp depth and 0.5 m cup depth; 50 cm is the inside opening width
